question: ‘Food, Work and Productivity’ were the focus of which Five-Year Plan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Seventh Five-Year Plan of India was from 1985 to 1990.
 
• The main objectives of the Seventh Plan were to establish growth in areas of increasing economic productivity, production of food grains, and generating employment opportunities.
 
• It aimed at accelerating food production, increasing employment opportunities, and raising productivity with a focus on ‘Food, Work, and Productivity’.
 
• During this plan, the economy experienced a significant growth in agriculture, industrial production, and employment generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans of India**

 
 
• Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs designed by the Planning Commission of India.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused on agriculture and irrigation to boost food production.
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) aimed at rapid industrialization and the development of heavy industries.
 
• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66) focused on agriculture and improvement in the production of wheat.
 
• Each subsequent plan aimed at different aspects of economic development, including alleviation of poverty, infrastructure development, and economic liberalization.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-90)**
 
 
• The Seventh Plan emphasized policies and programs that would accelerate food production, create employment opportunities, and increase productivity.
 
• It aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains and increase the production of pulses, oilseeds, and other essential food items.
 
• The plan also focused on improving the productivity of labor and ensuring better utilization of resources.
 
• During this period, significant growth was observed in agriculture, industrial production, and employment generation, which contributed to overall economic development.
 
 
 
• **Economic Planning in India**
 
 
• Economic planning in India is a mechanism for the allocation of resources between and within organizations which attempts to achieve the planned objectives.
 
• The Planning Commission was established in 1950, and it formulated Five-Year Plans to guide the economic development of the country.
 
• In 2014, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), which now acts as the policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• NITI Aayog aims to involve states in policy-making processes and promote cooperative federalism.
